$comment: Banned-pattern list for triage_group_findings.py (intent #4290, unit U9). Every body this pipeline authors is scanned against these patterns before it is filed, and a match is a hard failure — a GitHub issue is a permanently-retained artifact, so reproduction detail that reaches one cannot be recalled. The patterns are STRUCTURAL markers of reproduction detail (a request that can be replayed, a payload that can be pasted, a credential that can be used), not a keyword blocklist: naming a vulnerability class is the point of a work item, whereas showing how to trigger it is not.

patterns.reason: A replayable request. The single most common way an exploit reaches a document verbatim.
A verb-plus-path pair is a request, not a location. Name the module in `fix_surface` instead; the endpoint is in the ledger.
A header line carrying a credential, or the shape of one.
Announces reproduction detail. If the heading is present the detail follows.
An attack-tool invocation. Naming the tool is naming the recipe.
A JSON Web Token — a live session in a permanent document.
A GitHub, Slack or OpenAI-style token.
A credential with a concrete value attached. Describing that a secret is mishandled is fine; showing it is not.
